name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.netgum
top_fix: Disclose the silently-repaired compile error in src/Netgum.Domain/ValueObjects/EmailAddress.cs (backup line 30 had Python syntax `throw new DomainException(...) from ex;` so the solution could not build), and restore the inner exception with the two-arg DomainException ctor.
summary: Reorders CheckoutService so all deterministic validation runs before the payment-gateway call and before any tracked EF mutation, and makes CompleteOrderAsync return the persisted receipt early for Paid/Failed orders. 11 real xUnit cases over EF InMemory with the project's actual repositories assert tracked state (StockQuantity, RedeemedCount, Orders.Count) plus gateway/email/save counters; TRX and on-disk counts reconcile exactly at 11/11. Idempotency limits are stated correctly (application-level terminal-state idempotency is not an idempotency key). Main gap: a compile-breaking EmailAddress.cs line was fixed without any course mention, and there are no predict-then-run prompts.

name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.nethris
top_fix: De-golf server/Nethris.Api/HrisApi.cs: replace the 194-line hand-rolled path-splitting dispatcher (multiple statements per line, no MapGet/MapPost, no model binding) with idiomatic ASP.NET Core route groups, and port the highest-value scripts/check_api.py scenarios into WebApplicationFactory xUnit tests so `dotnet test` proves more than 13 of 61 claims.
summary: A 180-file rewrite of an HRIS that lands the full target CRUD curriculum on running code: strong ETags with If-Match, Idempotency-Key creation receipts with replay, transactional writes across domain+audit, role-sensitive field projection, pagination bounds, bounded org traversal and a two-stage captured-manager plus distinct-HR approval. Verification honesty is the batch's best (13+28+17+3=61 reconciles exactly, screenshots exist, limits admit the agent's own failed cleanup). The serious flaw is pedagogical: a 502-line idiomatic minimal-API Program.cs was compressed into a 194-line bespoke dispatcher, so the code the learner reads is not the ASP.NET Core they will write, and only 13 of 61 checks are xUnit.

name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.netpastebin
top_fix: Add a real xUnit project and port the version-conflict, missing-If-Match, receipt-replay and failed-replacement checks out of verification/BackendChecks/Program.cs into [Fact]/[Theory] tests; today `dotnet test` does not exist for this repo.
summary: The cleanest .NET code Astra produced (idiomatic MapGet/MapPut minimal API, proper Api/Domain/Data/Models layering) and the best-taught reliability lesson: optimistic concurrency with a required quoted If-Match, correct 428-vs-412 semantics, durable creation receipts for lost acknowledgements, cooperating-process file leases, and a React conflict flow that preserves the user's draft instead of discarding it. Checks are substantive (two spawned worker processes prove cross-process writes are not lost; a Windows sharing-failure test proves accepted bytes survive), counts reconcile exactly (30 Check() calls on disk = claimed 30; 15+30+17+14=76), the harness returns a real exit code, and nine screenshots exist. Caveats: zero xUnit, persistence is a JSON file with no EF Core (SQLite is only Ticket 4), and PasteWorkspace.jsx is 787 lines with three components.

name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.nettrello
top_fix: Convert tests/NetTrello.Checks/Program.cs into an xUnit project (one [Fact] per Expect* group, [Theory]/[InlineData] for the malformed PATCH bodies) and replace tests/http-regression.ps1 with WebApplicationFactory<Program> tests, removing the fail-fast masking, the PowerShell dependency and the DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major workaround.
summary: A short, technically excellent course on the most commonly-botched CRUD operation: HTTP PATCH. It fixes a DTO that turned 'field omitted' into 'field cleared' using the correct System.Text.Json approach (non-nullable JsonElement properties keyed on JsonValueKind.Undefined, [JsonUnmappedMemberHandling(Disallow)] for typo'd fields, Enum.IsDefined after Enum.TryParse), and fixes a real data-loss bug where Board.MoveCard removed a card from its source column before validating the destination. Checks snapshot the whole board before each rejected operation to prove nothing partially mutated, exercises demand predictions and expected-state tables before a separate solutions chapter, and the record is candid enough to name a field (board Version/UpdatedAt) its own assertions do not cover. No xUnit; the React client that sends the PATCH was never built or tested.

name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.netvg
top_fix: Fix the false C# claim in astraupskill/03-WORKED-CHANGE.md:12 that 'total uses `checked` addition' detects decimal overflow — checked/unchecked has no effect on decimal in C#; decimal always throws OverflowException. Also add a real midpoint test for the new MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero, which is currently unproven.
summary: Built around one excellent finding: the React client used to fabricate a successful quote from mock data whenever the API call failed, so a legitimate 400 rejection displayed a real-looking number to the user. Astra deletes that, teaches the correct ASP.NET Core ProblemDetails contract (detail -> title -> raw body), tightens the C# calculator boundary with Enum.IsDefined and ISO normalization, and adds a small RequestGate so a slow response cannot overwrite newer state. 14 xUnit cases and 3 deferred-promise Node tests reconcile exactly with the TRX (14/14) and the limits volunteer their own gaps. Two caveats: the course teaches a factually wrong rule about `checked` and decimal, and there is no database, EF Core or persistence anywhere — it is a stateless calculator, so it is an elective on validation and async races rather than a CRUD course.

name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.netzen
top_fix: Close the inconsistent enum guard — Ticket.Create still accepts (TicketPriority)99 while UpdatePriority rejects it (Astra disclosed this but shipped it) — and add a chapter showing how to push the authorization predicate into the query instead of the new loop that pulls every source page into memory on each search.
summary: Do this for one lesson most juniors have never been shown: authorization must be applied before pagination, not after. The original handler read the first 100 rows, then filtered by permission, then paged, so an authorized user's results past row 100 vanished and Total was wrong; a 121-ticket fixture proves the fix. It pairs that with a deferred-LINQ trap (_tags.Clear() followed by AddRange(lazyQuery) can half-apply, demonstrated with a deliberately-throwing iterator) and a SignalR redesign that stops broadcasting ticket payloads to a shared group in favour of a payload-free invalidation forcing each client to refetch through its authorized endpoint. Evidence is scrupulous (3 claimed, 3 on disk, 3 in TRX, with an explicit warning not to read the frontend build as a test pass). But only one of the four changes is tested, the new search loop should not be copied into EF Core, and the hub useEffect now tears down the SignalR connection on every filter change.

name: _Organized Desktop/02 Build Projects/buildasana
top_fix: Replace the child-process HTTP test (WorkManagementServiceTests.cs:162 spawns `dotnet run` on hardcoded port 51937 with --no-build and 40 readiness polls, resolving its working dir by walking '..' five times) with an in-process WebApplicationFactory<Program> test, and teach that tool in 04-TESTING-AND-DEBUGGING.md.
summary: A competent validation course whose best idea is the audit fix: the original emitted an `automation.executed` record even when no automation branch actually ran, and the course frames why an audit log that lies is worse than none. It also demonstrates the layering rule juniors most often collapse — throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException from the domain where a bad enum is a programming error, return a Result failure from the application service where it is user input bound for a 400 — plus reference-integrity checks before save+audit and materialize-before-mutate tag handling. 9 xUnit tests, TRX 9/9, exact match, with self-critical limits. Deductions: the HTTP test spawns a child dotnet run on a fixed port, the quoted normalizer contains an unreachable .Where clause, the in-memory dictionary store means nothing here teaches transactions or EF Core, and Astra knowingly retained the same fabricate-a-success frontend fallback it removed and condemned in .netvg.

name: _Organized Desktop/02 Build Projects/buildjira
top_fix: Remove the ApplyPatch <-> CopyMutableIssueFields coupling: the helper hand-lists 8 fields with no compile-time tie to the 8 body properties ApplyPatch reads, so a future ninth patchable field (Issue also has Type and SprintId) would be silently discarded behind a 200 response. Replace the object in the collection instead, and add an assertion that every settable field survives a valid patch.
summary: The sharpest bug story in the batch. UpdateIssue handed the live singleton Issue to its patch walker, so a request setting a valid title and then failing on storyPoints:101 returned a validation error with the title already changed in memory — and the next unrelated valid save wrote that leaked title to disk. Astra fixes it with clone -> validate -> copy-back and pairs it with the System.Text.Json trap juniors always hit: GetString() on a number and TryGetInt32() on a non-number both throw (a 500), so you must check ValueKind before the accessor to get a 400. The regression harness asserts unchanged file bytes, unchanged project timestamp, unchanged audit count, and that an unrelated later save does not make the rejected title durable. Evidence is reported at honest granularity (1 harness, 6 scenario groups, 9 malformed cases) rather than inflated. No xUnit anywhere, and the store is a JSON file so nothing teaches EF Core.
